conviction_note: Industrial (Motion) read-throughs are strong and NA commercial auto peers held up, but the guide needs a +15% yoy Q4 to hit its midpoint, diesel rose ~18% after the July guide that budgeted $20-30M of H2 freight/fuel, estimates are being trimmed and the stock ran +12.5% since the Q2 print; a modest negative lean (p_up 45) on a 5.5% absolute move, with the findings' own sum (-1.0) a little larger in magnitude because several small negatives stack.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS ~$2.04-2.05 on revenue ~$6.49-6.52B: Benzinga $2.05/$6.49B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GPC/earnings-forecasts), AAII $2.04 from 9 analysts with 1 down-revision and 0 up in the past month (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517849-what-you-need-to-know-about-genuine-parts-companys-q3-earnings, 2026-10-18). Company FY2026 guide adj EPS $7.50-8.00, GAAP $5.90-6.40, sales +3% to +5.5%, NA Auto +2.5-4.5%, Intl Auto +5-8%, Industrial +3-6% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000031/gpc-earnq22026.htm, 2026-07-21). Year-ago Q3 2025 adj EPS $1.98 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40987/000004098725000194/gpc-earnq32025.htm). print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.61M shares, 4.80% of float, 6.9 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09), down 16.2% from 7.90M at the prior settlement (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/GPC/short-interest). Elevated against March 2026 (2.42 days to cover, https://equibles.com/stocks/gpc/shortinterest) but not crowded and being covered. Baseline: 25d skew +2.38 vol points (mild downside paid), put/call OI 0.24 (call-heavy, plausibly residual takeover optionality from the July O'Reilly bid report), event-implied move 6.82% but ATM spread 42% of mid so indicative only; 20d run-up +4.85%, +12.5% since the 2026-07-21 print vs SPY +2.0% (AAII).

findings.finding: Industrial (Motion, ~37% of sales, Q2 comps +6.1%) read-throughs since GPC last spoke are strong: Fastenal Q3 2026 daily sales +15.5% with heavy manufacturing +20.2% (up from +12.4%) and pricing +240bp, ISM September PMI 54.5 (ninth month of expansion, new orders 55.3, prices 77.9), Applied Industrial June organic >10%; against a GPC Industrial full-year guide of only +3% to +6% this points to Q3 Industrial comps at or above Q2's +6% and room to raise the segment range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Industrial comps +6.1% with an EPS beat ($2.15 vs ~$2.08) and the stock fell -2.68% (baseline 2026-07-21) on the trimmed GAAP/NA auto outlook: segment strength has not been paid when the auto side or the guide disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($6.49-6.52B, ~+4% yoy) is consistent with Industrial near its 3-6% guide rather than the 6%+ the peer tape implies; if the market had priced an Industrial raise, revisions would be up, not 1 down / 0 up in the past month (AAII). Partly priced via the +12.5% run since July.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a GPC number. ISM: https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-pmi-reports/pmi/september/ ; Applied Industrial: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109563/000010956326000031/a8k8132026releaseexhibit991.htm ; GPC itself said Motion 'carried its June strength into July' (https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176). Net of the rest: Automotive is ~63% of sales and is where the cost headwinds below sit.

findings.finding: North American commercial auto demand held up in the peer prints since July: AutoZone domestic commercial +8.6% in the 16 weeks to 2026-08-29 with domestic comps accelerating to +2.1% in August after bottoming in June, while Advance Auto Parts Pro grew low single digits in its quarter to 2026-07-18 and DIY weakened; NAPA is mostly commercial and guided NA Auto +2.5-4.5% with July 'low single-digit'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA Auto range was cut to 2.5-4.5% in July and the stock fell -2.68%; the line moves the stock when it disappoints. No sourced instance of a NA Auto upside surprise being paid.
findings.why_not_priced: AutoZone's commercial share gains (+8.6%) may come partly from NAPA, so the read-through is ambiguous; it lands inside the guided NA range, so at most it removes a downside risk rather than adding a beat.
findings.independence: AAP Q2 2026 release (Pro LSD, DIY weak): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158449/000119312526357755/aap-ex99_1.htm. Proxy; O'Reilly (2026-10-28) reports after the window.

findings.finding: U.S. on-highway diesel rose from about $5.13/gal in mid-July and $5.31 the week of 2026-07-27 to ~$5.85 on 2026-09-04 and ~$6.05 on 2026-09-11 (vs ~$3.70-3.81 a year earlier); GPC's 2026-07-21 guide budgeted only $20-30M of incremental H2 freight and fuel cost from the Iran conflict, almost all in Automotive, so the fuel headwind in Q3/Q4 likely exceeds the guided range unless passed through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Iran-conflict EBITDA hit of ~$16M was 'in line' and the guide was held, yet the stock fell -2.68% on the outlook; Feb 2026 -14.56% on a cost-driven miss ($1.55 vs $1.82).
findings.why_not_priced: Diesel is public, but consensus Q3 EPS ($2.05, +3.5% yoy) and an unchanged FY bar imply nobody has marked GPC's freight line to September fuel; if they had, estimates would be falling faster than one down-revision in a month and the stock would not be +12.5% since July.
findings.independence: September level: https://northeasttimes.com/2026/09/11/diesel-surpasses-6-a-gallon-pushing-up-grocery-and-delivery-costs-nationwide/ (2026-09-11) and https://www.truckingdive.com/news/diesel-prices-surge-even-higher-due-to-iran-war-surpassing-538/815529/ ; GPC's $20-30M H2 guide: https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176 (Q2 call). Macro-to-company transmission, partly offset by management's stated ability to pass costs through and by ~2% pricing in the guide.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from GPC's own releases: H1 2026 adjusted EPS $1.77 + $2.15 = $3.92, so the $7.75 guide midpoint needs H2 $3.83 vs $3.53 in H2 2025 (+8.5%); with Q3 consensus $2.05 (+3.5% on $1.98) the implied Q4 is ~$1.78 vs $1.55 (+15%), against H1 growth of +1-2%. Management said in July that only 'absent second-half headwinds' would it track to the high end; the setup favours a narrowing to the lower half of $7.50-8.00, as the company did at Q3 2025 (narrowed to $7.50-7.75).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 narrowed the top end of the guide on a slight miss and the stock rose +2.05%; Q2 2026 held the adj guide but trimmed GAAP and NA Auto and fell -2.68%; Feb 2026 initial guide plus miss -14.56%. Mixed: narrowings have not always been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY sits near the midpoint (Q1 preview cited $7.73) while the Q4 step-up is unusually steep; if the market expected a narrowing, the stock would not have outrun SPY by ~10 points since the Q2 print.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 $1.77: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2904805/genuine-parts-q1-earnings-miss-estimates-on-costs-revenues-beat ; Q4 2025 $1.55: https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/genuine-parts-company-gpc-q4-2025-usd-adj-eps-155-exp-182-revenue-601bln-exp-606bln-lifts-quarterly-dividend-c-3-and-confirms-plans-to-separate-automotive-and-industrial-businesses-into-two-cos ; Q3 2025 $1.98: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40987/000004098725000194/gpc-earnq32025.htm. Counter: $100-125M of 2026 restructuring savings are H2-weighted and the Q4 2025 base held one-off vendor credit losses, so part of the step-up is mechanical.

findings.finding: The stock is +12.5% from the 2026-07-21 print to 2026-10-16 against SPY +2.0%, while Q3 estimate revisions over the past month are 1 down and 0 up (AAII revisions score 39, 'Negative'): price has run ahead of estimates into a print whose last beat was sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat sold -2.68% (intraday about -7% per the sweep); 2 of the last 3 prints negative.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; the claim is that the run raised the bar beyond the published consensus. The mild +2.38 put skew agrees, so it is partly priced.
findings.independence: Baseline run_up_20d +4.85%, 52w-high gap -11.2% (sealed baseline). Part of the run may be residual takeover optionality (finding on the O'Reilly bid), which shares the explanation.

findings.finding: Auto-parts peers are booking IEEPA tariff refunds in cost of sales (AutoZone ~145bp of Q4 gross margin, roughly $96M, in the quarter to 2026-08-29; Advance Auto $26M in the quarter to 2026-07-18, recognized when received), while GPC, a large importer, has disclosed no refund: EDGAR full-text search for 'IEEPA' and 'tariff refund' in GPC filings 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-19 returns zero hits; a first recognition in Q3 would be a gross-margin one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GPC history on this line. Across this repo's resolved days the same refund thesis split two up and two down by guidance direction.
findings.why_not_priced: No GPC disclosure, so no estimate carries it; but GPC may exclude it from adjusted EPS or pass it to customers, and Section 232 auto-parts duties are not refundable, so the value is small and uncertain.
findings.independence: AutoZone release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000117184326006159/exh_991.htm ; EDGAR search https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22IEEPA%22&ciks=0000040987 (0 hits). Inference about GPC, no company confirmation.

findings.finding: The Q2 FX tailwind (+1.4% of sales) has faded: EUR/USD traded about 1.15-1.16 through September 2026 against a 2026 year average of 1.165 and a June low of 1.1325, so International Automotive (~25% of sales) loses most of its translation help in Q3, a modest headwind to reported sales growth against a ~+4% revenue bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observed; FX is usually looked through.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue already implies only ~4% growth vs Q2's 6%, so analysts may have it; small.
findings.independence: Q2 FX contribution: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000031/gpc-earnq22026.htm. Year-ago Q3 2025 rate not sourced here, so this is inference.

findings.finding: GPC filed an automatic shelf (S-3ASR) on 2026-10-16 covering common, preferred, depositary shares and debt, proceeds for general corporate purposes including refinancing, acquisitions and buybacks, no selling holders; most plausibly a routine three-year shelf renewal and/or a vehicle for separation-related debt.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and generic; what it buys is the Q1 2027 separation capital structure, not distress (investment-grade issuer, FCF guide $550-700M). Signed zero after asking what the money is for.

findings.finding: O'Reilly reportedly bid ~$10B cash for the NAPA automotive unit in early July 2026; on the Q2 call management said it was not in discussions with any competitor, and on 2026-09-09 it named Court Carruthers CEO-elect of the post-spin automotive GPC and set investor days for 2026-12-08/09, signalling the spin path; any explicit closing of the door on the call removes residual takeover optionality that the call-heavy option open interest (put/call 0.24) may still hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock 'jumped' on the July bid report (https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/insight/genuine-parts-jumps-on-10b-o-reilly-bid-for-auto-unit/gm-GM858FEF77); no print-day history.
findings.why_not_priced: Ambiguous: if optionality were fully gone the call-heavy OI and the +12.5% run would look different; if it were fully priced, a confirmation would be a positive. Wide band both ways.
findings.independence: CEO-elect 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40987/000119312526385959/d136093d8k.htm (2026-09-09); call remark: https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176. Shares the run-up explanation with the positioning finding.

findings.finding: Short interest is 4.8% of float and 6.9 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about three times the 2.42 days to cover of March 2026, though down 16% from mid-September: a modest short base that cushions a negative reaction and adds fuel to a positive one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced squeeze history on GPC prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning, not information; it is a mechanism on the reaction. Not crowded enough for a large squeeze.

outside_window.finding: Separate investor days for automotive GPC (2026-12-08) and Motion (2026-12-09) in New York, where standalone targets and capital structures will be given.
O'Reilly Q3 2026 results 2026-10-28 and Advance Auto Parts Q3 2026 results 2026-11-05, the next NA auto read-throughs.

Any status update on the O'Reilly NAPA bid after July 2026
GPC EDGAR full-text for 'IEEPA' / 'tariff refund' in 2026 filings (0 hits)
Confirmation that the Form 10 for the separation has been filed (none found)
MSC Industrial fiscal Q4 2026 actuals (not yet reported; only its guide of ADS +6.5-8.5%)

rejected_candidates.candidate: AutoZone fiscal 2027 domestic comps guide flat to low single digit on ~4% ticket growth
rejected_candidates.detail: Same AutoZone release and call as the NA commercial read-through finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: MSC Industrial fiscal Q3 2026 ADS +7.8% and Q4 guide +6.5% to +8.5%
rejected_candidates.detail: Another industrial MRO proxy pointing the same way as the Motion finding; merged rather than counted twice.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q2 2026 call: $100-125M 2026 transformation savings, H2-weighted, and expected H2 gross margin expansion
rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into the guide-arithmetic finding as its counterweight rather than filed as a separate positive.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the mild +2.38 put skew (downside paid) and cuts against the call-heavy open interest and the +12.5% run since July; the negative lean is small because the industrial tape is strong and short interest has tripled since March.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; Q2 beat was sold): Motion read-through cut from +1.2 to +0.8.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy, unconfirmed transmission) and lesson 9 (net of pass-through pricing): diesel finding cut from -1.2 to -0.8.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs, refund thesis split by guidance): tariff-refund finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): S-3ASR kept at 0 after asking what it funds.
Lessons 6 and 7 left the rest standing: bar sourced from three agreeing estimates, short interest checked and a squeeze cushion filed; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
